input.quote: 7.2 Customer shall offer Vendor terms no less favourable than the best terms Customer offers any other technology supplier.
input.rationale: Section 7.2 imposes an open-ended MFN running against us: we would have to extend Silverline the best terms we offer any other technology supplier, with no product scope, time limit, or comparison carve-outs. That is the playbook walk-away position (MFN is acceptable only in the Customer's favour). It also conflicts with § 12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no most-favoured-customer commitment. The minimal fix is to delete the standalone obligation; no other clause depends on it and no Vendor-granted MFN is affected.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have deleted the requirement that we extend Silverline the best terms we give any other technology supplier — our playbook does not permit MFN obligations running against us, and § 12.3 already confirms we make no most-favoured-customer commitment. MFN pricing in our favour remains welcome; if some form of reciprocity is essential, we could consider an MFN limited to a single named product for 12 months with reasonable-comparison carve-outs.
